decisions.decision: Use Fulk’s vowel-specific breaking conditions and æ as the immediate input; Cook’s own qualification is preserved, not labelled an error.
Distinguish older e-raising from later i-umlaut, while recognizing the established practical mutation grouping.
Use actual course spellings as learner examples. Preserve Fulk’s dotted originals in the source audit and record any removal of editorial dots, thorn/eth substitution or hook notation explicitly.
The local asterisk means reconstruction, unlike the explicitly erroneous examples of Unit3; use escaped literal stars. Arrows mean historical development, never a sequence of principal parts.

Existing headwords cover all selected OE examples. Three supplied additional source spellings (hefon, hēafodes, hēh) have explicit appendix routes; original glossary masters, data and acceptance remain unchanged.
Define vowel length separately from historical syllable/stem weight; qualify high-vowel loss and analogy.
Omit a full PIE/Proto-Germanic reconstruction course, exhaustive consonant laws, nasal-loss/metathesis catalogues and formal exercises. Core breaking/umlaut explanations take priority.
